newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-Palestinian violence mars peace mission.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-Palestinian violence mars peace mission.

text.p: Bullets and rocks flew in the Gaza Strip while an Egyptian envoy toiled with little apparent success to bring Israel and the Palestinians closer to resuming formal peace talks.

Only Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose decision to start work on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March plunged Middle East peacemaking into crisis, seemed confident the impasse could be broken.

"I am convinced that within a short time we will overcome all the obstacles and resume the peace process with our Palestinian neighbours in order to accelerate the talks on a permanent peace settlement," he said in a speech on Thursday.

Netanyahu, who spoke in northern Israel after meeting Egypt's envoy Osama el-Baz in Tel Aviv, has proposed moving immediately into so-called final-status talks that would tackle issues such as Jewish settlements and the future of Jerusalem.

But Palestinians, who have accused the right-wing leader of trying to avoid handing back more occupied land under interim peace deals, have demanded that Netanyahu must stop the East Jerusalem project before full-fledged talks can resume.
"We will continue more consultations and contacts in the coming period," Baz told reporters after meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the self-ruled town of Ramallah in the West Bank.
"We hope that this...in a positive spirit will lead to a breakthrough in the situation that would allow the peace process to be preserved," he said.
But Baz's mission was clouded by clashes that erupted in two locations near Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip after several months of relative calm in the area.

Israeli soldiers shot and wounded two Palestinians during a clash with hundreds of Arabs protesting against the building of a fence for the Jewish settlement of Morag on land claimed by Arabs, witnesses said.
Israeli military sources said soldiers and Palestinian police dispersed hundreds of rock-throwing demonstrators. They made no mention of casualties.
An elderly Palestinian died at a protest tent on the site, apparently from a heat attack, a doctor at the Khan Younis hospital said.

Palestinians later stoned Israelis at the Gush Katif block of Jewish settlements in another part of the Gaza Strip when they gathered for a ceremony dedicating a memorial to an Israeli soldier killed in clashes in September, witnesses said.
Khaled Abu Ila, a Palestinian officer, told Reuters that during the clash a "young settler" fired his weapon randomly, wounding two more Palestinians.
"Jewish settlers fired towards rock-throwers. There were no casualties," the Israeli army said.

Israel stationed two tanks out of sight of Palestinians close to the Gush Katif trouble spot. Israel Television showed the tanks on its evening news, a signal from the Israeli army that if Palestinian police did not keep order, it would.
Brigadier-General Yoav Galant, commander of Israeli forces in Gaza, said the current situation was "tense and sensitive."
